# Lab 19.17: Review AI Findings in SCC

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn on AI Protection in Security Command Center, explore the AI inventory, and review an AI-specific finding.

## Steps

1. **Check the tier.** AI Protection needs Security Command Center **Premium** or **Enterprise** at organization level. Open **Security → Security Command Center → Settings** and check your tier.

2. **Turn on AI Protection.** In **Settings → Services**, find **AI Protection** and set it to **Enabled**. Data can take some hours to appear.

3. **Create something to find.** Use the Gemini call from Lab 19.8 so the project uses a Gemini model without Model Armor.

4. **Open the AI Security dashboard.** Go to **Security Command Center → AI Security**. Review:
   - **AI inventory**: models, agents, endpoints and datasets found
   - **Sensitive data in AI resources**, from Sensitive Data Protection
   - **AI findings** grouped by severity

5. **Review a finding.** Open a finding such as a model not protected by Model Armor. Read the **Description**, **Affected resource** and **Next steps**.

6. **Query findings with gcloud.**

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud scc findings list organizations/ORG_ID --location=global \
  --filter='state="ACTIVE"' \
  --format="table(finding.category,finding.resourceName,finding.severity)" | grep -i -E "model|agent|ai"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


7. **Fix and confirm.** Apply a Model Armor template or floor setting (Lab 19.15). After the next scan, the finding becomes **Inactive**.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| AI inventory | Models, agents and AI data listed |
| Findings | AI-specific categories with fixes |
| Tier needed | SCC Premium or Enterprise |
| After fixing | Finding moves to Inactive |
